title.value: HalluciDet: Hallucinating RGB Modality for Person Detection Through Privileged Information
title.justification: The title is directly mentioned in the paper as its main focus and it is part of the document header.
title.quote:
HalluciDet: Hallucinating RGB Modality for Person Detection Through
Privileged Information

analysis.description: The paper introduces HalluciDet, a novel approach that enhances person detection in infrared (IR) images by leveraging pre-trained RGB detectors to guide the translation process from IR to RGB modality. The proposed model enhances object detection performance by using hallucinated RGB representations that incorporate privileged information from pre-trained models in the RGB domain. This model is empirically compared against existing image translation and IR tuning methods, demonstrating improved detection accuracy.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical comparisons and experimental results using IR-RGB datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed HalluciDet model.
type.quote:
We empirically compare our approach against state-of-the-art methods for image translation and
for fine-tuning on IR, and show that our HalluciDet improves detection accuracy in most cases by exploiting the privileged information encoded in a pre-trained RGB detector.

name.justification: The paper is centered around visual recognition models and image translation, which are primary concerns in the field of Computer Vision.
name.quote: In this paper, we propose HalluciDet, an IR-RGB image translation model for object detection.

name.justification: The focus of the paper is on improving detection accuracy of objects (persons) in infrared images using models pre-trained on RGB images.
name.quote:
Our translation approach relies on an annotated IR dataset and an RGB detector to
identify the appropriate representation space. The ultimate goal is to find a translation model, hereafter referred to as the Hallucination network, capable of translating IR images into meaningful representation to achieve accurate detections with an RGB detector.

name.justification: The paper discusses a model based on IR-RGB image translation to enhance object detection performance.
name.quote: We propose HalluciDet, a novel approach that leverages privileged information from pre-trained detectors in the RGB modality to guide end-to-end image-to-image translation for the IR modality.

name.justification: The approach involves adapting a model trained on RGB images to perform effectively on IR images, which is a domain adaptation problem.
name.quote: In this work, we provided a framework that uses privileged information of an RGB detector to perform the image-to-image translation from IR.

name.justification: The paper introduces a model named HalluciDet specifically for translating IR to RGB images for detection tasks.

adversarial loss, and U-net is based on reconstruction loss.

name.justification: The LLVIP dataset is one of the primary datasets used for evaluating the proposed model.
name.quote:
The LLVIP dataset is composed of 30, 976
images, in which 24, 050 (12, 025 IR and 12, 025 RGB
paired images) are used for training and 6, 926 for testing
(3, 463 IR and 3, 463 RGB paired images).
